html:
SMTO-EXE-0271 — This workflow run stopped before it finished

GUID: 7400c4f9-946d-546b-945e-ea7eaf6cc08b
Slug: recipe-execution-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • The workflow stopped partway through. Steps that already finished were not undone, and a step that was running when it stopped may or may not have taken effect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the stopped run: in Schedules, or in Workflows under History, select Open run. Or go back to the conversation where it ran. The run's conversation shows which steps finished and which never started.
  2. For each step that changes something, such as sending, saving or deleting, check the real result yourself, for example look for the file or message it was meant to create. Stopping doesn't undo finished steps, and a step cut off midway may already have taken effect.
  3. Only when you know what is still missing, start the workflow again, for example with Run now. A new run repeats every step, so starting it before checking could make the same change twice.

What success looks like

  • The new run finishes without repeating work that was already done.

If it still fails

  • If you can't tell whether a step took effect, don't run the workflow again. Select Copy error details and send it, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A workflow run was cancelled (retained recipe.execution_cancelled kind; current code records cancellation through generic run cancellation and per-step operation receipts, with no compensation).

What this means

  • This retained workflow cancellation kind has no direct current producer in the recipe implementation; generic cancellation and operation receipts determine the actual stop and effects. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • This retained workflow cancellation kind has no direct current producer in the recipe implementation; generic cancellation and operation receipts determine the actual stop and effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect task cancellation state and each original step receipt before deciding what remains.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cancelled run's step states (recipe run history metadata step_states, written by recipes.runtime.observe and sync_history) and the original operation receipts. Treat completed and outcome_unknown steps as possibly applied and settle them before starting a separate new run; cancellation never rolls back completed effects.
  • Inspect and settle the original cancelled run before starting distinct new work; never assume cancellation undid completed steps.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The original run is settled and any completed or uncertain effects remain recorded.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
